 J U D G M E N T
MANJULA CHELLUR,CJ

Though appeal is filed challenging interim order dated 02/08/2012,
Sri.Deepak Dhingara, learned Senior Counsel for the appellant submits that the grievance of the appellant is only with regard to ambiguity at Ext.P7 by not using the words 'tobacco' and 'nicotine' in the products like 'gutkha', 'panmasala' or like articles.
2. The argument of learned senior counsel is considered.
We have also gone through the observation of learned Single Judge so far as this aspect of the matter is concerned.

At the time of seeking interim relief, the stand of the appellant and others was different and now the only clarification they want is to remove the ambiguity at Ext.P7 because such ambiguity could lead to disastrous consequences by putting impediment or restriction on the sale of any article which can be called as 'panmasala' though it does not contain 'Nicotine' or 'tobacco'.
Third and last paragraphs of Ext.P1 are relevant in order
to understand what was the intention of the department while issuing notification dated 22/05/2012.

"AND WHEREAS the Commissioner of Food Safety of the State is empowered under Section 30 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 to prohibit in the interest of public health, the manufacture, storage distribution or sale of any article of food in Dharampal Satyapal Limited vs State Of Kerala on 2 August, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185749978/
2 the whole of State.
NOW, THEREFORE in pursuance of regulation 2.3.4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011, the manufacture, the storage, the sale or the distribution of gutkha and panmasala containing tobacco or nicotine as ingredients, by whatsoever name it is available in the market, is hereby prohibited in the State of Kerala in the interest of Public Health."

sentences.text: 3. By reading these two paragraphs, it is very clear that the intention of the department was to prohibit 'gutkha' and 'panmasala' in the State of Kerala being food products in which tobacco or nicotine are widely used and so also similar or like products in which tobacco and nicotine are ingredients.
By the time communication to Designated Officers came to be issued by the Commissioner of Food Safety on 25/05/2012, there seems to be missing of important words 'nicotine' or 'tobacco'.

Letter dated 25/05/2012 at Ext.P7 reads as under:
"As per order referred as above (copy attached) Commissioner of Food Safety has banned production, distribution and sale of gutkha and panmasala like articles by whatever name called in the State.
Hence, you are directed to take urgent steps to effect the ban under your jurisdiction with immediate effect and also further issue necessary instruction strictly to all food business operators.
The products banned may be seized if necessary from the godown itself and get it sealed to assure effective ban in the State.
Government will be directing Dist.Collector and Commissioner/Superintendent of Police to form squads for enforcing the prohibition.
Action taken report should be submitted within one week without fail."
3. Reading of the first paragraph indicates that production, distribution and sale of gutkha and panmasala and like articles by whatever name called in the State of Kerala is banned.
Ext.P7 dated 25/05/2012 is a communication of the order dated 22/05/2012 at Ext.P1.
As a matter of fact, the real intent is not imported in the letter dated 25/05/2012.

4. Therefore, it is made clear that the intention of the department in issuing Ext.P7 was to prohibit or ban production, distribution and sale of 'gutkha' and 'panmasala' containing 'tobacco' or 'nicotine'
as ingredients, by whatsoever name they are available in the market in the State of Kerala.
With this clarification, this appeal is disposed of.
